name: Bellhop recurring jobs
description: Recurring definitions (code-, runtime- and configuration-defined), startup reconciliation, the atomic trigger on NextRunAt, misfire and overlap policies, time zones and DST, and runtime management. Each occurrence that starts creates a job in the jobs module.

entities.name: Occurrence
entities.description: One due instant of a recurring job and what was done about it.

ears.shall: give every recurring job an explicit IANA time zone, UTC when none is given
use RunOnce as the default misfire policy and Skip as the default overlap policy
record each recurring job's origin as code (attribute or AddRecurring), runtime (IRecurringJobManager or dashboard) or configuration (Bellhop:RecurringJobs)

ears.when: a node starts and a code-defined recurring job has no stored definition with its name
ears.shall: create the definition with its schedule, time zone, policies and payload, and nextRunAt computed from now

sources.quote: On startup each node MUST upsert code-defined recurring jobs idempotently by name.

ears.when: a node starts and a code-defined recurring job's stored definition differs from the code
ears.shall: update the stored definition to match the code, keeping its paused or active state

requirements.notes: Keeping the paused state is my reading. Open questions: (1) during a rolling deploy, nodes on versions N and N+1 may hold different definitions of the same job and will overwrite each other at every start; which wins? (2) if the job has AllowRuntimeOverride and was edited at runtime, does a restart overwrite the edit?

ears.shall: never hold two recurring definitions with the same name, and never fail a node's startup because another node is reconciling the same definitions at the same moment

sources.quote: Multiple nodes starting simultaneously MUST NOT create duplicates or throw.

ears.when: a node starts and a stored code-defined recurring job is no longer declared in code
ears.if: the orphan policy is the default
ears.shall: mark the job orphaned, which also pauses it, instead of deleting it

requirements.notes: Open questions: (1) during a rolling deploy the old version re-creates or updates the job (REQ-203, REQ-204) while the new version orphans it, so the state can flip on every start; (2) what brings an orphaned job back when the code declares it again (REQ-206)?

sources.quote: A code-defined job removed from code MUST be marked Orphaned and paused, not deleted (configurable).

ears.when: a node starts and an orphaned recurring job is declared in code again
ears.shall: make the job active again with nextRunAt computed from now

requirements.notes: Gap: not in the source; without it Orphaned is a dead end. Ask the owner.

ears.when: a node starts and a stored code-defined recurring job is no longer declared in code
ears.if: the orphan policy is set to delete
ears.shall: remove the definition

requirements.notes: Same event as REQ-205 with the complementary guard. The source only says the orphan behaviour is 'configurable'.

ears.when: an operator adds a recurring job through IRecurringJobManager or the dashboard and no definition with its name exists
ears.shall: create a runtime-defined recurring job with nextRunAt computed from now

ears.if: a schedule expression given through the API or the dashboard is invalid
ears.shall: reject the call with an error that says what is wrong and store nothing

sources.quote: Invalid expressions MUST fail ... at the API call (runtime-defined), never silently.

ears.if: a code-defined recurring job has an invalid schedule expression
ears.shall: stop the node from starting with a message that names the job and the expression

sources.quote: Invalid expressions MUST fail at startup (code-defined)

ears.if: an operator edits a code-defined recurring job through the API or the dashboard and the job is not marked AllowRuntimeOverride
ears.shall: reject the edit with a message saying the job is defined in code

requirements.notes: Open question: does 'edit' include pause, resume, trigger now and remove? Pausing a code-defined job from the dashboard seems intended (CON-5) but is an edit of its state.

ears.when: an operator updates a runtime-defined recurring job, or a code-defined one marked AllowRuntimeOverride
ears.shall: store the new definition

ears.when: an operator removes a recurring job
ears.shall: delete the definition

requirements.notes: Open question: removing a code-defined job at runtime would be undone at the next start (REQ-203). Is remove refused for code-defined jobs like edit (REQ-211)?

ears.when: an operator pauses a recurring job through the API or the dashboard
ears.shall: mark the job paused

ears.when: an operator resumes a paused recurring job
ears.shall: mark the job active and compute nextRunAt from now

requirements.notes: 'From now' is my reading, by analogy with REC-10. Open question: are occurrences missed while paused subject to the misfire policy (a RunOnce catch-up on resume) or simply dropped?

ears.while: a recurring job is paused or orphaned
ears.shall: never create an occurrence for it on schedule

requirements.notes: 'Trigger now' (REQ-226) on a paused job is not covered by the source.

ears.where: a recurring job has a validity window
ears.shall: never create an occurrence on schedule before ActiveFrom or after ActiveUntil

ears.when: its nextRunAt has passed according to the database clock
ears.shall: in one compare-and-set on nextRunAt, advance nextRunAt to the next occurrence after now and create the occurrence or occurrences its misfire policy calls for

sources.quote: Triggering MUST be an atomic compare-and-set on the stored NextRunAt so that N nodes produce exactly one occurrence.

ears.shall: create at most one occurrence for each due instant of a recurring job, however many nodes run the scheduler

ears.when: a recurring job is triggered after one or more due instants were missed
ears.shall: create a single catch-up occurrence for all missed instants

requirements.notes: Open question: when is an instant 'missed' rather than just a little late? A node polling once per second is always slightly late; a threshold (misfire tolerance) is needed so that Skip does not drop on-time runs. Ask the owner.

ears.when: a recurring job is triggered after one or more due instants were missed
ears.shall: create no occurrence for the missed instants and only advance nextRunAt to the next future occurrence

ears.when: a recurring job is triggered after one or more due instants were missed
ears.if: the misfire policy is RunAll with a maximum
ears.shall: create one occurrence per missed instant, up to that maximum

requirements.notes: Open question: when more instants were missed than the maximum, are the oldest or the newest kept?

ears.when: a recurring job is triggered after one or more due instants were missed
ears.shall: log how the missed instants were handled and why, and raise the recurring-missed event

requirements.notes: The event is consumed by notifications (REQ-403) and IJobEvents (REQ-169).

ears.when: an occurrence is created and no earlier occurrence of the same recurring job is still running
ears.shall: enqueue a job with the recurring job's payload and record the occurrence as started

requirements.notes: Recurring jobs may carry a payload, so one job type can have many recurring instances, for example one per tenant (REC-8). Open question: 'still running' is not defined. Does a previous occurrence that is Failed (waiting to retry) count?

ears.when: an occurrence is created while an earlier occurrence of the same recurring job is still running
ears.shall: start nothing and record the occurrence as skipped

sources.quote: Skip (default: do not start if the previous run is still active; record a Skipped occurrence)

ears.when: an occurrence is created while an earlier occurrence of the same recurring job is still running
ears.shall: record the occurrence as waiting for the earlier one to finish

requirements.notes: Open question: if a run lasts several periods, do waiting occurrences pile up without limit, or is at most one kept?

ears.when: the earlier occurrence's job succeeds, is dead-lettered or is cancelled
ears.shall: enqueue a job for the waiting occurrence and record it as started

ears.when: an occurrence is created while an earlier occurrence of the same recurring job is still running
ears.if: the overlap policy is Allow or CancelPrevious
ears.shall: enqueue a job for the new occurrence and record it as started, and under CancelPrevious also request cancellation of the earlier occurrence's job

requirements.notes: Under CancelPrevious the two runs overlap until the earlier handler honours its token.

ears.where: a recurring job's overlap policy is Skip or Queue
ears.shall: never have two of its occurrences' jobs processing at the same time on any nodes

requirements.notes: Expected to fail when a lease expires and the job is recovered while the original node still runs it (the at-least-once window, REQ-10). The model should report that case.

sources.quote: enforced by the store across nodes

ears.shall: never fail a job, throw an exception or wait on a lock timeout because of an overlap decision

sources.quote: No distributed lock timeouts, no exceptions.

ears.when: an operator triggers a recurring job now, optionally with an overridden payload
ears.shall: create an occurrence immediately using the overridden payload if one was given

requirements.notes: Open questions: does the overlap policy apply to a manual trigger (all three outcomes listed until answered)? Does it change nextRunAt? Is it allowed while the job is paused?

ears.when: a recurring job's schedule changes
ears.shall: compute nextRunAt from now, never from the last execution, and create no catch-up occurrence for the old schedule

ears.when: a recurring job's next occurrence falls on a local time skipped by a daylight-saving change
ears.shall: run it once at the next valid instant

ears.when: a recurring job's next occurrence falls on a local time repeated by a daylight-saving change
ears.shall: run it once

requirements.notes: Open question: once at the first or the second instance of the repeated time? And does an interval schedule (Every) follow wall-clock or elapsed time across DST?

ears.when: an operator asks for a recurring job's next N occurrences
ears.shall: compute them from its schedule in its own time zone

ears.when: an occurrence's job succeeds, is dead-lettered or is cancelled, or an occurrence is skipped
ears.shall: record that outcome as the recurring job's last outcome

ears.where: recurring jobs are defined in configuration under Bellhop:RecurringJobs
ears.when: that configuration changes
ears.shall: apply the added and changed definitions without a restart

requirements.notes: Open questions: what happens to a definition removed from configuration (orphaned like code, or deleted)? Are configuration-defined jobs read-only in the UI like code-defined ones? With several nodes, which node's configuration wins?

sources.quote: Recurring jobs MAY also be defined in configuration (Bellhop:RecurringJobs) with IOptionsMonitor hot reload

scenarios.title: Two nodes, one occurrence
scenarios.given: nightly-cleanup is active with nextRunAt 03:00; nodes A and B both poll at 03:00:00.

steps.note: B tries the same compare-and-set on the old nextRunAt

scenarios.title: Overlap Skip records a skipped occurrence
scenarios.given: A job runs every minute with overlap Skip; the 10:00 run is still processing at 10:01.
scenarios.then: The 10:01 occurrence is Skipped, no second job was enqueued and the 10:00 job is still the only one processing.

scenarios.title: Schedule change creates no catch-up
scenarios.given: A job runs hourly; last run 09:00; at 09:30 the schedule changes to daily at 08:00.
scenarios.then: nextRunAt is 08:00 tomorrow and no occurrence was created for 08:00 today or for 10:00.

scenarios.title: Removed from code becomes orphaned, not deleted
scenarios.given: weekly-report is stored as code-defined and active; a new release no longer declares it; orphan policy is the default.
scenarios.then: weekly-report is Orphaned, still stored, and creates no occurrences.

scenarios.title: Dashboard cannot edit a code-defined job

steps.note: operator changes the schedule from the dashboard

scenarios.title: RunOnce catches up once after downtime
scenarios.given: An hourly job with misfire RunOnce; all nodes were down from 01:30 to 05:10.
scenarios.then: Exactly one catch-up occurrence was started, the miss was logged with its reason, and nextRunAt is 06:00.

scenarios.title: Simultaneous startup creates one definition
scenarios.given: An empty store; nodes A and B start at the same moment, both declaring nightly-cleanup in code.

steps.note: B tries to create it too

glossary.misfirePolicy: RunOnce (default: one catch-up), Skip (jump to the next future occurrence) or RunAll(max) (REQ-217 to REQ-219).
glossary.overlapPolicy: Skip (default), Queue, Allow or CancelPrevious (REQ-221 to REQ-225).
glossary.Orphaned: A code-defined job no longer declared in code; kept and paused (REQ-205).
